title: Measure the process-scan refresh cost in a release build
body:
Process-scan refresh: proc::Scanner::refresh in src/proc.rs. agent_for calls it at most every REFRESH_EVERY (1.5 s) from the tab-icon path (Session::icon_kind), on the UI thread. Close requests also force it via refresh_now.

Known numbers (2026-10-06, debug build, about 430 processes): the sysinfo refresh_processes_specifics call with with_cmd(UpdateKind::Always) took about 20 ms. The creation_time sweep added in card o6kzlr cost about 1 ms. Both are debug numbers. Nobody has measured release, so it is unknown whether this is a visible frame hitch every 1.5 s.

Do (predict, then measure; see foreman-proof-and-analysis-toolkit Recipe 4 and foreman-diagnostics-and-tooling for throwaway-harness patterns):
1. Write the prediction down first.
2. Time Scanner::refresh in a release build, split into the sysinfo call and the creation_time sweep. Use a temporary harness built with --release --target-dir target/agent. Never use cargo test --release, and never kill a running foreman.
3. If it is over about 2 ms, fix the cost at its source. Options: re-read command lines only for new PIDs (UpdateKind::OnlyIfNotSet), or move the refresh off the UI thread. Re-measure after.
4. If it is under that, record the number and close with no code change.

Acceptance: before and after release numbers, dated, with the setup, in the commit body. Also add a line to docs/tab-icons.md under "Process scan is throttled". Any fix keeps the recycled-PID guard (is_child_of / creation_time; docs/close-confirm.md, "Recycled parent PIDs") working, and keeps the proc:: tests green.

Gate: cargo build --target-dir target/agent; cargo test --target-dir target/agent; cargo fmt --check
